handbookNote: Source: official 'Minnesota Driver's Manual' (June 2026 edition), published by the Minnesota Department of Public Safety, Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) division, fetched directly from the .gov-hosted PDF at assets.dps.mn.gov/files/dvs/dvs-class-d-drivers-manual-english.pdf (linked from dps.mn.gov/divisions/dvs/license-and-id/class-d-regular-dl/class-d-dl-forms-documents-and-manuals). Full text extracted to temp/handbooks/mn/driver.txt (245KB, 8 chapters plus a 'New laws and information' section) and used as the sole factual basis for every question. Real exam mechanics researched directly from this manual: passing score is explicitly confirmed at 80 percent ('You may take only one written test per day and must score 80 percent to pass' -- Ch.1, p.10). The written test format is confirmed as multiple choice and true-or-false questions, offered on paper or computer, in English, several other languages, or ASL. The exact number of test questions is NOT stated anywhere in the official manual, and could not be confirmed from the DPS/DVS website pages checked (main DVS page, Class D license page, forms-and-manuals page, FAQ page all lack this figure; general web search was unavailable this session after budget exhaustion) -- this figure is left unconfirmed rather than guessed, per project convention. No time limit for the written test is mentioned anywhere in the manual, so the test is treated as effectively untimed for practice purposes, though this absence-of-mention is not the same as an official confirmation of 'untimed' status. Content depth: Minnesota's manual is unusually rich and detailed (8 full chapters covering licensing/GDL, vehicle equipment, traffic laws, sharing the road, signs/signals/markings, driving conditions, driving privileges, and DUI/alcohol/drugs), each with many specific, quotable numeric facts (distances, fees, percentages, ages, time periods). This supported writing 271 grounded, non-repetitive multiple-choice questions across 16 topic buckets without any invented facts or padding; every question cites the specific manual section and page. All questions are traceable to specific manual text -- none were invented or borrowed from another state.
